paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: two women are calling out to the same people, and they open with the SAME words. "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!" (Proverbs 9:4, 16). The invitations sound alike, but the tables are not. One leads to life, and the other leads to a place where "the dead are there" (Proverbs 9:18).

So how do you tell them apart? Wisdom says, "Leave your folly behind, and you will live" (Proverbs 9:6), and the passage says that "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom" (Proverbs 9:10). Folly just says the secret stuff tastes good, and she never mentions where it ends up. I've been in a place where nobody told me the whole story, and I'd rather hear it from the one who sets a table out in the open.

Wisdom is also a gift you get to keep, and the passage says "If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage" (Proverbs 9:12). Being willing to be taught makes you wiser still (Proverbs 9:9). So pull up a chair at the right table, baker, and stay hungry to learn. And if you know you lack judgment, good news: that's exactly who she's inviting.
